description: B1'S GUARD OPEN AT ITS STAIR (DECK-GUARD-OPENING; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B1, docs/BACKLOG.md STAIRS, IRC R312, Chief Architect's deck railing): B1 at loft.deck 1.3.0 with its guard on the open sides (4x4 posts, 2x4 rails, 2x2 balusters, 36 in) and every other default, and b1-stair-30's loft.stair 1.0.0 centred on the rim at X 96, 36 in wide. The stair offers its inputs to the deck it picks, and 1.3.0 breaks the front guard between the stair's outer stringer faces, X 78 to X 114, with a post each side. model.json is EXACTLY the two expansions with their member materials; members.json is each body's member metadata with its plugin (packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_deck_guard_opening.py pins both; services/geometry/tests/test_deck_guard_opening_b1.py checks the STEP against an independent build123d script, the opening, interference and the cut list).
derivation: INDEPENDENT of the plugins: test_deck_guard_opening_b1.script() is test_stair_b1's B1 (71 735.979474 in^3: buildings.md's 64 497.75 of framing and decking and 3 piers of 768 pi) and its stair (4 062.891133 in^3, b1-stair-30's derivation), and the guard typed here from buildings.md B1 and IRC R312. The STEP matches the 159 solids solid for solid (volume to 1e-4 in^3, bounds to 1e-5 in).

the guard stands on the decking (Z 30..66), along the left (X 0..3.5), front (Y 140.5..144) and right (X 188.5..192) sides. Posts on a run lo..hi: one at each end, equally spaced at most 72 in apart. The left and right sides are one run, 0..144: posts at Y 1.75, 72, 142.25, two bays of 66.75 clear. The front is broken at the stair's outer stringer faces, X 78 (its left stringer 78..79.5) and X 114 (112.5..114): runs 0..78 and 114..192, posts at X 1.75, 39, 76.25 and 115.75, 153, 190.25 (76.25 - 1.75 = 74.5 > 72, so two bays a run), so a post 74.5..78 and one 114..117.5, each face on its stringer's; four bays of 33.75 clear. Posts: 3 + 3 + 4 not at a corner = 10 (the closed guard's 8).

rails, 2x4 on edge 1.5 across, Z 33.5..37 and 62.5..66, between the posts: a course is 66.75 x 4 + 33.75 x 4 = 402 in, the front's 192 - 36 (the opening) - 6 x 3.5 (its posts) = 135 against the closed guard's 192 - 4 x 3.5 = 178: 43 in less a course, 86 over the two (890 -> 804 in). Balusters 2x2, Z 37..62.5: ceil((clear - 4) / 5.5) a bay, equally spaced: 12 in a 66.75 bay (3.75 gaps), 6 in a 33.75 bay ((33.75 - 9) / 7 = 3.5357 gaps), 4 x 12 + 4 x 6 = 72 (the closed guard's 81).
surface_area, centroid, mass_g and center_of_mass are the script's solids summed (test_deck_guard_opening_b1.expected_numbers()): southern_pine_pt 582 and concrete 2400 kg/m^3 (loft_wire.materials).

topology from the script's B-rep: b1-stair-30's 378 faces, 768 edges and 61 shells plus 98 boxes of 6 faces and 12 edges (10 posts, 16 rails, 72 balusters): 966, 1 944, 159; the kernel's build of model.json meets every count exactly. MESH counts are recorded, not derived (b1-stair-30's 3 036 / 2 280 plus 98 boxes of 24 vertices and 12 triangles: 5 388 / 3 456, as measured).

Interference none (test_deck_guard_opening_b1.test_nothing_interferes probes every pair whose boxes overlap, exactly): the posts each side of the opening stand on the decking (Z 30) with their faces in the planes X 78 and X 114 of the outer stringers, which hang under it (Z <= 29) from the rim's face at Y 144; the stair's handrail posts (X 74.5..78) start at its top nosing, Y 146.125, 2.125 past the guard post's face at Y 144.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). The bounds are ABSOLUTE and the part is ~1.45e9 mm^3 summed over 159 bodies: the kernel differs from the script by -7.2e-6 mm^3 on the volume (5e-15 relative, the summation's ULPs over 159 solids; b1-stair-30's 61 give -1.2e-6), 1.5e-8 mm^2 on the area, <= 5.9e-12 mm on the centroid and centre of mass and 1.4e-9 g on the mass. 3e-5 is 4.2x the volume's; a baluster missed takes 9.4e5 mm^3 (57.375 in^3) and a post moved 1/16 in moves the centroid 7.9e-3 mm, so either fails by more than two orders.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: KERNEL-LEVEL, measured 2026-10-29, b1-stair-30's class: OCCT's STEP writer rounds the three notched stringers' and the sloped handrail's irrational coordinates (the slope 7.5/11 and L), and the 159 re-imported solids sum in another order. Round-trip drift: volume -3.8e-6 mm^3, area +6.7e-7 mm^2, centroid 1.5e-11 mm (plugin); the independent build123d twin (test_deck_guard_opening_b1.script(), exported with build123d's export_step) drifts -3.1e-5 / -9.5e-7, so it is OCCT's STEP, not Loft's export. 1e-4 is 3.2x the worst (the twin's); it applies to volume and area only, the centroid and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL.
